A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAGE work. All 24 pages in each version, including appendix Sections 6–9, figures, tables, equations and prompts, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAGE-Bench and MINERVA experiments, runtime measurements, ablations and qualitative reasoning examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Video-MMMU, Video-MME and per-tool evaluation results.

M1.justification: The two-stage orchestrator, six supported tools, synthetic-data pipeline, SFT procedure and GRPO rewards are unchanged. Newly tested tool restrictions are ablation conditions, without a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained SAGE-Bench and MINERVA evaluations, v2 adds actual testing on Video-MMMU for knowledge acquisition and perception-focused Video-MME. These benchmarks previously appeared only in contextual discussion and illustrative examples, so the additions substantially broaden external evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in retained experiments is unchanged. New Table 6 reuses Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and Video-R1-7B, all already evaluated in v1, extending existing comparison methods to the added benchmarks.

E3.justification: The added experiments specify Video-MME without subtitles and introduce single-tool, no-tool and combined tool-removal controls. Reported SAGE-Bench counts are corrected: open-ended questions change from 944 to 942 in Table 4, and the 2400+ second bucket changes from 180 to 160 in the statistics and duration tables. These corrections do not establish changed samples or reruns.

E4.justification: New Table 18 tests tool sufficiency using individual-tool and no-tool configurations, extending the retained leave-one-tool-out analysis. New Table 6 also tests removing ground-event alone or together with extract-video-parts on both added benchmarks. Earlier ablations remain intact.

E5.justification: The five-run Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct analysis at temperature 1.0 is unchanged, including mean 64.9 and standard deviation 0.22, moving from Table 16 to Table 17. No new repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure is supplied.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantive cross-benchmark findings: Table 6 reports SAGE-Flash at 68.1 on Video-MMMU versus Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct's 65.3, but 63.5 versus 66.8 on Video-MME. Removing both specified visual tools yields 61.8 and 66.2 respectively. Table 18 adds individual-tool results, including 61.1 for transcription alone and 53.0 without tools. Retained SAGE-Bench and MINERVA performance scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The trajectory formulation and reward equations in Section 3 are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about any-horizon reasoning, synthetic-data generation, RL training and SAGE-Bench. The new experiments extend supporting evidence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly attributes harmful visual-tool use on Video-MME to its perception-focused tasks. Appendix Section 6 explains dependencies between tools and adds specific failure conditions: retries exhausting reasoning steps, inaccurate grounding omitting relevant segments, and misleading transcript or web information.

D1.justification: Implementation details, training hyperparameters, hardware, inference handling, system prompts and the repository link are unchanged. The new experiments disclose evaluation controls but add no corresponding implementation or resource-access information.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 64 works and retain the related-work discussion and novelty positioning. Video-MMMU and Video-MME were already cited; their additional experimental citations do not introduce new related works.

P1.justification: v2 adds short generalization, per-tool accuracy and failure-analysis passages, with corresponding cross-reference updates. Existing sections and their narrative order remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 inserts main-text Table 6 and appendix Table 18, renumbers intervening tables and locally reflows surrounding text. Existing figures and table designs are retained; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added benchmarks strengthen external validation while revealing a Video-MME weakness, and the per-tool tests and failure discussion improve diagnostic transparency. Corrected sample counts also remove inconsistencies. These provide a limited overall quality improvement: the new evidence usefully qualifies applicability, although uncertainty reporting is not strengthened.
